statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96233 (GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Runtime: DateTime parsing of Hebrew numbers can read outside expected stack bounds and terminate the process. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix is in the DateTime parser of System.Private.CoreLib (dotnet/dotnet commit d9b2f326d2829d4e741404a24b6fce979733f20e on release/10.0.1xx; the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.113 source tag, from which the 10.0.13 runtime and SDK 10.0.113 are built, contains it and v10.0.112 does not: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/d9b2f326d2829d4e741404a24b6fce979733f20e). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll at its own .NET version, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the runtime pack, NativeAOT pack and runtime archives held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap (seven copies per build and architecture); no copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

That version is 9.0.12 to 9.0.20 in the first eight builds and 9.0.21 or later from 9.0.21-r0 on. The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96233 (GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Runtime (System.Private.CoreLib): DateTime parsing of Hebrew numbers can read outside expected stack bounds and terminate the process. Microsoft lists the .NET 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. The .NET 9 fix is dotnet/runtime commit 01e241f190d0b31abb222aa21f98404143960251 on release/9.0 ("Fix DateTime parsing with Hebrew characters"), a merge whose changes outside tests are confined to the DateTime parser, DateTimeParse.cs; it is in the v9.0.21 tag and not in v9.0.20: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/01e241f190d0b31abb222aa21f98404143960251. DHI dotnet-sdk-9 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 9 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0, 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-9 and dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-9 build carries one System.Private.CoreLib.dll, in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>; no other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. Its version is 9.0.17 in 9.0.315-0, 9.0.18 in 9.0.316-0 and 9.0.316-1, 9.0.19 in 9.0.317-1, 9.0.20 in 9.0.318-0 and 9.0.318-1, 9.0.21 in 9.0.319-0, 9.0.22 in 9.0.320-0 and 9.0.23 in 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, the same on both architectures. Every copy records the dotnet/runtime commit it was built from: the v9.0.17 to v9.0.20 tags in the builds up to 9.0.318-1, and the v9.0.21, v9.0.22 and v9.0.23 tags from 9.0.319-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 9.0.319-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
